Natural_Language: As used in this part -- Exception means an approved departure from the established design, content, or conditions for use of any standard form.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_001_a: An Exception is an approved departure from established design of any standard form; P_53_001_b: An Exception is an approved departure from established content of any standard form; P_53_001_c: An Exception is an approved departure from established conditions for use of any standard form
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. 'Design, content, or conditions' is disjunctive per explicit 'or'. Biconditional appropriate for definitions (X is defined as Y means X <-> Y). Each element independently qualifies as an exception.

Natural_Language: Policy regarding forms usage encompasses requirements, forms list, continuation sheets, and exceptions.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating four policy subsections. All four components constitute the complete policy framework for Part 53 forms.

Natural_Language: The requirements for using the forms are contained in parts 1 through 52, where the subject matter applicable to each form is addressed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_101_a_a: Requirements for using forms are contained in FAR Parts 1 through 52; P_53_101_a_b: The subject matter applicable to each form is addressed in the respective part
Validation_Notes: Declarative statement establishing that form usage requirements are distributed across Parts 1-52 rather than centralized in Part 53. Broad external reference to Parts 1-52 not trackable as specific dependency.

Natural_Language: A list of the standard forms (SF), optional forms (OF), and agency forms specified by the FAR for use in acquisitions is available at https://acquisition.gov/FARforms. The list identifies the forms' current edition location, FAR part requirement, and prescribing agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_101_b_a: A list of SF, OF, and agency forms specified by the FAR is available at acquisition.gov/FARforms; P_53_101_b_b: The list identifies forms' current edition location; P_53_101_b_c: The list identifies FAR part requirement; P_53_101_b_d: The list identifies prescribing agency
Validation_Notes: Declarative/descriptive statement. Serial commas for list content ('edition location, FAR part requirement, and prescribing agency') treated as conjunction per default rule. All elements describe attributes of the forms list.

Natural_Language: SFs prescribed in the FAR may be continued on plain paper of similar specification, or specially constructed continuation sheets (e.g., OF 336). Continuation sheets must include both the reference number of the document being continued and the serial page number in the upper right hand corner.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_101_c_a: SFs prescribed in the FAR may be continued on plain paper of similar specification; P_53_101_c_b: SFs prescribed in the FAR may be continued on specially constructed continuation sheets (e.g., OF 336); P_53_101_c_c: Continuation sheets must include the reference number of the document being continued; P_53_101_c_d: Continuation sheets must include the serial page number in the upper right hand corner
Validation_Notes: First sentence is permissive ('may') with disjunctive options (plain paper OR continuation sheets). Second sentence is mandatory ('must') with conjunctive requirements ('both...and'). Combined: choice of medium is permissive, but regardless of medium chosen, both identification requirements are mandatory.

Natural_Language: Agencies must obtain an exception from the form's prescribing agency. For SFs prescribed by the FAR, agencies must obtain an exception from the FAR Council.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_101_d_a: Agencies must obtain an exception from the form's prescribing agency; P_53_101_d_b: For SFs prescribed by the FAR, agencies must obtain an exception from the FAR Council
Validation_Notes: First sentence is general mandatory requirement. Second sentence adds conditional: when the SF is FAR-prescribed, the specific approval authority is the FAR Council. HIGH-RISK flag due to Material Implication. The conditional narrows the general rule for a specific subset. Dependency on P_53_001 for definition of 'exception'.

Natural_Language: Computer generation of FAR-prescribed forms is permitted under specified conditions.
Validation_Notes: Parent with single substantive subsection (a). Section only contains 53.105(a) with its sub-paragraphs.

Natural_Language: The forms prescribed in the FAR may be computer generated without obtaining an exception (see 53.101(d)), provided that one of the following conditions is met.
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' but structured as conditional permission: IF either condition (1) or (2) is met, THEN computer generation is allowed without exception. 'Provided that' is conditional trigger with disjunctive conditions (connected by 'or' at end of (1)). HIGH-RISK due to Material Implication. Cross-reference to 53.101(d) creates dependency.

Natural_Language: There is no change to the name, content, or sequence of the data elements, and the form carries its number and edition date.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_105_a_1_a: There is no change to the name of the data elements; P_53_105_a_1_b: There is no change to the content of the data elements; P_53_105_a_1_c: There is no change to the sequence of the data elements; P_53_105_a_1_d: The form carries its number; P_53_105_a_1_e: The form carries its edition date
Validation_Notes: Negation atomics represent 'no change to' requirement. 'Name, content, or sequence' uses 'or' but in context of 'no change to' means none of these may change (conjunctive prohibition). 'And' connects the no-change requirement to the number/date requirement. Both conditions must hold simultaneously.

Natural_Language: The form is in an electronic format covered by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) X12 Standards published by the Accredited Standards Committee X12 on Electronic Data Interchange or a format that can be translated into one of those standards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_105_a_2_a: The form is in an electronic format covered by ANSI X12 Standards published by ASC X12 on EDI; P_53_105_a_2_b: The form is in a format that can be translated into one of the ANSI X12 Standards
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive condition: either native ANSI X12 format OR translatable into ANSI X12 satisfies the requirement. Explicit 'or' makes disjunction clear.

Natural_Language: Recommendations concerning forms may be submitted by the public and government personnel through designated channels.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two recommendation channels: public and government. Both pathways constitute the complete recommendations framework.

Natural_Language: FAR users may recommend new forms or revisions, elimination, or consolidation of existing forms identified on the forms list (see 53.101(b)). These recommendations should be submitted to the FAR Secretariat.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_108_a_a: FAR users may recommend new forms; P_53_108_a_b: FAR users may recommend revisions to existing forms on the forms list; P_53_108_a_c: FAR users may recommend elimination of existing forms on the forms list; P_53_108_a_d: FAR users may recommend consolidation of existing forms on the forms list; P_53_108_a_e: Recommendations should be submitted to the FAR Secretariat
Validation_Notes: First sentence is permissive ('may') with disjunctive recommendation types. Second sentence uses 'should' (advisory, not mandatory) for submission channel. Marked PENDING_REVIEW per 'should' override rule. Cross-reference to 53.101(b) forms list.

Natural_Language: Recommendations from within an executive agency must be submitted to the cognizant council in accordance with agency procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_108_b_a: Recommendations from within an executive agency must be submitted to the cognizant council; P_53_108_b_b: Submission must be in accordance with agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Conditional: IF recommendation originates from within executive agency, THEN must submit to cognizant council AND follow agency procedures. 'Must' makes both requirements mandatory. HIGH-RISK due to Material Implication.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.253-1, Computer Generated Forms, in solicitations and contracts that require the contractor to submit data on SFs or OFs; and, unless prohibited by agency regulations, forms prescribed by agency supplements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_53_111_a: Insert clause 52.253-1 in solicitations and contracts requiring contractor data submission on SFs; P_53_111_b: Insert clause 52.253-1 in solicitations and contracts requiring contractor data submission on OFs; P_53_111_c: Insert clause 52.253-1 for forms prescribed by agency supplements unless prohibited by agency regulations
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause insertion ('Insert') triggered by contractor data submission requirement. SFs and OFs are disjunctive triggers. Agency supplement forms have additional conditional: permitted unless agency regulations prohibit. 'Unless' = negation conditional. External dependency on clause at 52.253-1. HIGH-RISK due to multiple Material Implications.
